comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel reports a modest aggregate increase in its 'All Other' segment revenue (+$78 million), AMD reports a massive surge in its primary Data Center segment revenue (+94% to $12.6 billion). Both disclose specific product drivers for their respective growth: Intel cites improved supply enabling backlog fulfillment for Altera and higher demand for Mobileye EyeQ products, whereas AMD cites higher sales of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. Intel's growth is fragmented across smaller non-reportable segments with offsetting decreases, contrasting with AMD's concentrated, high-growth narrative in its core reporting segment.

sentences.text: All other revenue was $5.6 billion, up $78 million from 2022.
Altera revenue was $2.9 billion, up $314 million from 2022, driven by improved external supply, which enabled the fulfillment of customer backlog.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Total revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60.9 billion, representing a 126% increase from the previous year.
comparisons.comparison: Intel reports a relatively small absolute revenue increase of $78 million in its 'All Other' segment, reflecting stable but slow growth in niche areas. In contrast, NVIDIA reports a total revenue increase of 126% ($60.9 billion), driven by explosive demand in the AI infrastructure market. While both companies operate in the broader semiconductor space, Intel's disclosed segment shows incremental, supply-constrained recovery, whereas NVIDIA's disclosure highlights a fundamental structural shift in revenue magnitude driven by AI accelerators, illustrating vastly different scales of market expansion.
